anim_framing: A character animation sprite sheet for a 2D top-down survival game: a grid of {cols} columns and {rows} rows of equally spaced frames on a transparent background. Top row: the character facing the camera and to the right (front 3/4 view); bottom row: the same character facing away from the camera and to the right (back 3/4 view). Camera moderately above, about 30 degrees down (not top-down). Identical character, proportions, clothing and lighting in every frame, full body visible in every frame, feet on one baseline per row, frames in time order left to right. No text, no frame, no border, no ground, no cast shadow.

assets.desc: the same muscular broad-shouldered man (athletic heavy build: wide shoulders and chest, thick neck and arms, narrow waist, strong legs, normal-sized boots), short dark hair, stubble, square jaw, wearing a worn quilted khaki telogreika jacket over a dark t-shirt, dark grey work trousers and brown boots, standing still at ease, holding a long hunting carbine LOWERED at low ready with both hands (right hand on the grip, left hand under the fore-end), muzzle pointing down at the ground a step ahead, relaxed shoulders, subtle breathing — NOT aiming, carbine NOT raised. The attached image has two parts. LEFT: a grey mannequin grid — use it ONLY as the pose, timing and camera reference, copy each frame's pose exactly. The mannequin holds only a placeholder; paint a real AK held correctly with both hands as described. RIGHT: the painted character — copy his face, hair, clothes, boots and colours exactly; do not include the reference figure itself. REALISM IS THE PRIORITY: correct human anatomy and joint angles, believable weight and balance, feet actually touching the ground, natural hand grip on objects, consistent body size in every frame; upright confident posture (not hunched). Gloomy post-Soviet survival, muted desaturated natural colours (olive, khaki, grey-brown), hand-painted like Project Zomboid and Rust, soft overcast light from the top-left, strong readable volume.
